title: One shared heavy forward and multi-Mirror output transport with grouped offload overlap
scientific_questions: Under which exact equivariance or factorization conditions are four/five logical expert outputs obtainable from one heavy shared execution and cheap Mirror transforms?
When global/hidden Mirror acts before a nonlinear activation, does the base output preserve sufficient information for cheap reconstruction? Test explicit collision and fresh heldout distortion.
How much common FFN computation can be saved by caching preactivation versus only output versus recomputing all views?
Given transfer T_io, compute window and predictor accuracy, does grouped multi-Mirror execution hide transfer versus equally proactive ordinary grouped/non-grouped offload controls?

hypotheses.H1_exact: For pure output-transport views and value-only attention, single-forward decoded outputs equal direct per-view evaluation within 1e-10 float64/3e-5 float32; preactivation-reuse hidden Mirror also equals direct evaluation while base output-only generally does not.
hypotheses.H2_approx: Output-only ridge/MLP transport can approximate hidden nonlinear views only where heldout functional difference is contained in the base output. No blanket claim of exact multi-View amortization.
hypotheses.H3_perf: Under CPU eager implementation and K=4/5, measured cost of sharing preactivation is lower than K independent full FFN evaluations on >=4/5 fresh worlds for B=128; latency of output-only exact views is separately benchmarked, and same-byte linear decoder baseline has priority.
hypotheses.H4_overlap: In a predeclared two-buffer deterministic event simulator, forwarding a group for longer can hide more transfer, but net tokens/s improves only if the reuse computation saved exceeds transfer/prefetch/false-prediction overhead. Compare oracle lookahead and realistic imperfect prefetch with a native pre-gated competitor.

mechanism.mirror_angles: independent pairwise angles uniformly within [-0.8,0.8] rad
mechanism.network: W_down GELU(W_up x) with hidden pairwise rotations inside nonlinearity
learned_readouts: ridge affine from y0 to each hidden Mirror output, λ in 1e-3; same-byte ordinary linear head
small MLP optional only after ridge source/dev gate, 100-150 updates fixed before fresh

prefetch_simulator.model: deterministic simulated two-buffer nonblocking DMA model with serial transfer stream and exact demand miss penalty, not measured physical PCIe
native_controls: ordinary linear-factor group with matched bytes and compute
Mirror grouped prefetch with same predictor/hardware

attention.value_only: same keys and queries, V_m=V B_m; attention distribution invariant; exact o_m=o_0 B_m
attention.key_transform: K_m=K A_m with q fixed changes attention probabilities, query GEMM/softmax not generally reusable
attention.coupled_transform: q_m=q (A_m^T)^(-1), K_m=K A_m makes query-key scores invariant, value readout output transformation only

gates.PASS_algebra: All five fresh numerical worlds satisfy shape, exact output-only/value-only/compatible q,k transport and shared-preactivation equals full per-view recompute at float64 <1e-10 or float32 <=3e-5; show explicit non-reusable counterexample in every world.
gates.FAIL_algebra: Exact identities fail, or output-only recovery asserted when same base output maps to two distinct hidden-view outputs.
gates.PASS_perf_screen: Paired CPU B=128, K=4 and K=5 shared-preactivation time <=0.90 K-full baseline median on >=4/5 worlds and difference doesn't disappear against cheapest direct output-only or native linear-code baseline in claims of Mirror-specific advantage.
gates.FAIL_perf_screen: Any claimed shared-preactivation speedup vanishes under matched native linear factorization, training-specific decoding produces worse latency, or CPU time not consistently lower at fixed workload.
gates.PASS_overlap_mechanism: At some pre-registered physically feasible simulated IO budget and predictor hit>=0.9, two-buffer Mirror grouped schedule reduces calculated transfer-related stall relative to on-demand by >=50%; report matched proactive native group baseline even if no Mirror-specific speedup.
gates.FAIL_overlap: No cost case wins end-to-end over equal-factorized pre-gated control, or H4 relies on oracle router lookahead without labeling it oracle.
gates.UNCERTAIN: No actual GPU/PCIe measurement; downstream LM quality not measured; numerical statistical evidence insufficient. These remain necessary for adoption.

negative_controls: output collision y0(x1)=y0(x2) while hidden view differs
key-only attention transformation with unchanged q
scope_limits: One shared forward is exact only when all desired outputs factor through the cached statistic; view address choice or knowledge of router outcome does not establish this.
Cache storage reuse is not compute reuse; key transform changes QK scores/softmax unless coupled query and key actions preserve logits.
Both output-only and global transformed models need their own training/fitting for useful specialist diversity; output-only factorization may reduce reachable functions.
Prefetch is existing work, including Pre-gated MoE; special claim is saved physical transfer bytes or useful longer compute window after fair amortized view computation.
No CUDA available in current container; memory transfer schedules are simulation, not measured overlap or GPU speedup.
